chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, from 'Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, regarding the word of the Most High:
'And We send down from the sky blessed water' [Quran 50:9]
He said: 'There is no water on earth except that the water of the sky has mixed with it.'

key_terms.السَّمَاء: The sky/heaven — both the physical sky and the realm from which divine blessings descend
key_terms.خَالَطَهُ: Has mixed with it — the verb indicating that heavenly water has mingled with earthly water, conferring blessing upon it
key_terms.مَاءً مُبَارَكاً: Blessed water — referring to rainwater sent from heaven, which the Quran describes as carrying divine blessing

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the blessing of rainwater in Islam?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrates that Imam al-Baqir (AS) transmitted a hadith from the Prophet (SAWW) offering a commentary on Quran 50:9, which refers to the sending down of blessed rain from heaven. The Prophet explained that every water on earth has been mixed with the blessed water that descends from the sky, thereby extending the sanctity and blessing of heavenly water to all earthly water sources. This hadith has relevance to discussions of water purity in Islamic jurisprudence.
